plan: [ This is a sealed-bid, second-price auction. The dominant strategy is to bid my true private value: bidding higher risks overpaying if a competitor’s bid lies between my value and my inflated bid; bidding lower risks losing when I would have profited. With no informative history and only 1 round, I should bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. My value is 49, so I bid 49. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding truthfully (bid = value) is a weakly dominant strategy. It maximizes expected profit because your bid only determines whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). Underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable; overbidding risks paying above value if others bid high. With value 44 and no informative history (single round), bid 44 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 44 and pay that second-highest price. ]

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. There’s no prior history to exploit. By bidding 22, we win exactly when the second-highest bid is below 22 and pay that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Any bid shading only risks losing profitable wins without reducing payment when we would win. Bid exactly 22 (0.1 increments allowed). Ties, if any, are random.
